newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down after 5-day winning streak.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down after 5-day winning streak.

text.p: Tokyo stocks buckled under profit-taking pressure on Tuesday, putting an end to the five-day winning streak. Brokers said profit-taking battered the Nikkei average for most of the day, but sentiment was still firm and the falls well cushioned.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 fell 93.43 points or 0.43 percent to 21,462.97. Its December futures were down 70 points at 21,500.
"The Nikkei average had five days of gains and technical alarms were starting to ring," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities.

"Most of the market believes that after the election, trade in incentive-backed speculative shares will make way for issues with solid reasons to buy or sell on," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.
"Speculative buyers are trying to rake in profits before the market mood changes," he added.
Shares in Oji Paper, which was formed today after New Oji Paper and Honshu Paper Co Ltd merged, were up four yen at 849 yen.
In the over-the-counter (OTC) market, Takefuji Corp fell on loss cut sales by investors.
The shares were down to 8,880 yen, after falling as low as 8,600 yen. On Monday it closed at 9,010 yen. The OTC index was down 9.44 points or 0.60 percent at 1,566.71.

Sector-wise, the decliners were transportation equipment, iron/steel, rubber, gas and fisheries. Air transportation, miscellaneous manufacturers, railway/bus, construction and textiles were the main gainers.

The second-section index was down 2.05 points at 2,107.1 on turnover of 12.75 million, against 8.73 on Monday. Turnover was estimated at 332 million shares compared to a very modest 268 million on Monday on the first section. --M.Iijima
